_: This project's bash whitelist. Copied to .claude/whitelist/rules.json by
install.py — edit it there, by hand, and never let an agent widen it.
extends    the profiles this rests on. base is not optional.
vars       values the profiles interpolate; a list becomes an escaped
alternation, a string is inserted as regex SOURCE.
disable    inherited rule ids to drop (see --show-rules for the ids).
allow      what THIS project runs: its verify gate and its reviewed scripts.
unmatched  what a command no rule vetted becomes: allow, agent or human.
"human" is the default and asks about everything unvetted.
escalate   unvetted commands that still ask the human: they delete,
overwrite, discard git work or publish. Extend it with whatever
destroys data in your toolchain before trusting "allow".
opaque     unvetted commands refused to the agent with rewrite help: code
the gate cannot read.
cases      every rule you add gets one case that must pass and one that
must NOT — the second is the reason anyone can trust the rule.
route_cases  what an unvetted command routes to: human, agent, allow, deny.
Check your work without running anything:
python3 .claude/hooks/bash-whitelist.py --self-test
python3 .claude/hooks/bash-whitelist.py --explain '<some command>'
python3 .claude/hooks/bash-whitelist.py --show-rules

escalate.why: deletion owes the human what, why now, what breaks and the way back
can discard uncommitted work or rewrite what a ref points at; `checkout X` is a branch switch or a file revert depending on X
publishes to a shared remote the team sees
writes over a file without reading it first
a database client can drop or delete rows
changes the machine, its processes or its permissions

opaque.why: runs a script or a string the gate cannot read
opaque.instead: run its commands directly, one per call, so each one is judged; or a reviewed script under .claude/scripts

opaque.why: runs an executable file the gate cannot read
opaque.instead: run the commands it contains directly, or a reviewed script by its allowed path

opaque.why: an interpreter runs code the gate cannot read; the allowed forms already passed
opaque.instead: python3 -c '…' under py-inline-guard, or a reviewed script by its path

opaque.why: a build runner executes recipes the gate cannot read
opaque.instead: run the recipe's commands directly, or the project's verify gate

allow.note: already covered by the node profile; kept here as the shape to copy for a project whose gate is spelled differently

Reviewed scripts by EXACT name — never a glob over scripts/. A glob would let an agent write a script and then run it. Each one validates its own arguments, does one job, and is write-protected in settings.json.
